correctness.rationale: For the explicitly defined 26-vertex incidence graph, same-type distances are 0 or 2, opposite-type distances 1 or 3. A 26-bit separating-mask test exhausts all 657800 seven-subsets (none resolving) and all 1562275 eight-subsets (exactly 9828, all balanced). A separate 13-choose-4 squared incidence-signature implementation obtains exactly the same total and four geometry profiles. Five explicit graph-automorphism generators form a group of order11232; orbit BFS exhausts all 9828 winners with orbit sizes936,1404,1872,5616. Both actual source files were executed and checked. Exact bounded finite proof; no extrapolation beyond PG(2,3).

originality.rationale: The full relevant 2012 primary article establishes the q=3 metric dimension eight and only classifies 4q-4 resolving sets for q>=23; Bailey reports only dimension eight in a table. The new claim is the 9,828 count, forced 4+4 balance and four full automorphism orbits with induced incidence geometries. Equivalent formulation and stronger-coverage searches found no matching implication or exact table. Published-record searches did not surface a covering record; absence of hits is not proof of novelty and unindexed prior enumeration remains a stated risk.
residual_risks: A previously unindexed metric-basis enumeration, supplementary data, or author code may contain these exact four orbit counts.
The literature search is finite and cannot prove universal absence of equivalent published statements.

value.rationale: The classical q=3 dimension-eight fact leaves open the natural classification of all optimal landmark configurations. The 9828 configurations separate into exactly four full projective symmetry types; their forced 4+4 balance and four distinct selected incidence structures are a natural geometric refinement, especially because large-q optimum-set descriptions require q>=23. The known split semi-resolving minimum twelve gives context for why point-line cooperation matters. This provides a reusable exact benchmark for finite-geometric metric identification, not an arbitrary parameter slice or a claim that the known dimension itself is novel.
